mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals improving labor market conditions, which positively impacts consumer and business confidence, leading to increased equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns during periods of declining UNRATE, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism is below 0.03 in out-of-sample testing.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) crosses above 4.5%, it indicates tighter monetary conditions, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns in > 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism is below 0.03 in out-of-sample testing.

mechanism_narrative: When both GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) show positive growth, it signals strong demand in both consumer and residential sectors, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns during periods of positive GDP and housing starts growth, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism is below 0.03 in out-of-sample testing.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals improved supply chain efficiency and increased economic output, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns during periods of industrial production growth, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism is below 0.03 in out-of-sample testing.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real estate investment (RSAFS) signals strong demand in the real estate sector, which positively impacts related industries and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns during periods of increasing real estate investment, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism is below 0.03 in out-of-sample testing.

mechanism_narrative: When the number of paid employees (PAYEMS) grows at a rate exceeding 0.5% month-over-month, it signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 5-day returns in > 40% of instances where PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5%, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism is below 0.03 in out-of-sample testing.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns during periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and UNRATE < 5%, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism is below 0.03 in out-of-sample testing.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals reduced inflationary pressures, leading to increased consumer purchasing power and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns during periods of declining CPI, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism is below 0.03 in out-of-sample testing.
